note: The clearest ICP mismatch in the batch and the closest thing in the corpus to the profile the stated definition explicitly rules out. The source quote says 'It's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight and I hate working out' — and this prospect describes not being able to lift his own body weight, finding every current session painful, and having struggled to put socks on because of abdominal fat to the point of feeling he was suffocating. Not_deconditioned and good_to_great both fail on that basis; his goal is to be able to walk, breathe and play with his children, which is rescue by any reading. Successful fails on the criterion as written: a salaried software engineer working nine to five is not a business owner, physician or equivalent. Income fails on the evidence he gave — audible shock at the price, a maximum of $2,000 available now, a French tax bill of roughly 2K a month arriving in two months, three young children and an explicit refusal to commit at a level that removes his contingency margin. Neglected_health is the single match and it is genuine: no diagnosed disease, just years of letting it go — 'I abandoned myself a little bit for some years.' The finding worth carrying up is the inconsistency it reveals rather than the mismatch itself. Three days before this call the rep proactively disqualified Nik Howe, a five-of-five ICP match with no financial constraint, from the $6,000 product and routed him to the $1,000 self-paced platform. Here a prospect failing four of five criteria was taken through the full flagship pitch and a $6,000 ask. Whatever rule is being applied, it is not the stated ICP, and it is producing opposite outcomes for opposite profiles.
